These results indicate that phonetic-category-based decomposition offers a scalable and transferable alternative to accent-level adaptation.

items.title: First-to-Spike: An Early-Exit Framework for Rapid and Energy-Efficient Spiking Neural Networks
items.abstract: Spiking neural networks offer a promising path to energy-efficient AI, yet their potential for low-latency inference often remains unrealized. Existing early-exit SNNs typically rely on extrinsic, non-spiking criteria like confidence thresholds, complicating the model. We revisit this paradigm by demonstrating that SNNs possess an intrinsic early-exit capability. We introduce the First-to-Spike framework, where inference terminates immediately upon the first spike from a competitive output layer. This event-driven mechanism is further accelerated by a Winner-Take-All circuit and optimized by a novel Hybrid Temporal Training objective. Extensive evaluations on speech and neurophysiological datasets show that F2S sets a new state of the art, achieving higher accuracy with significantly reduced latency and energy consumption. Our work validates that the spike itself can serve as a robust and efficient decision signal for real-time applications. Source code is available online.

title: Speech Recognition, Enhancement and Real-Time Systems

items.title: A light weight Continuous Speaker Verification System for Real time Monitoring
items.abstract: Continuous verification of customer identity during telephone interactions is essential to prevent unauthorized access to personal information in medical insurance applications and banking scenarios. We propose a real-time speaker verification system that continuously monitors customer's speech and compares it with an enrolled voice-print to detect speaker changes during an active call. Upon mismatch, the system generates alerts on the agent interface to prevent disclosure of sensitive information. The proposed method uses a two stage architecture with a ReDimNet-B1 backbone and a projection network trained with triplet sampling for robust speaker embedding extraction. Cross-lingual, noise, and reverberation-based data augmentation techniques are used to improve robustness. The system operates in real time with RTF 0.05 and a low computational footprint of 318M MACs. The model achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 2.08% on TidyVoice evaluation dataset, demonstrating strong robustness.

items.title: WaveNorm: A Low-Complexity Time-Domain Neural Adaptive Gain Control for Real-Time Speech Applications
items.abstract: We present WaveNorm AGC, a lightweight, low-latency neural Adaptive Gain Control(AGC) system for real-time speech normalization on edge devices. Operating in the time domain, it learns a content-aware, level-invariant gain mapping directly from raw waveforms. Unlike conventional rule-based AGC, it avoids fixed control parameters and hand-crafted envelope tracking, providing stable and responsive gain adjustment. WaveNorm AGC provides robust performance across a wide dynamic range upto -70 dB maintaining loudness compliance with ITU-T P.56 and P.79 standards under noisy conditions, while achieving ~6 dB noise reduction. The model is speaker-independent and highly efficient (49 M MACs, 55 KB of memory), making it suitable for real-time deployment on resource-constrained devices.

items.title: Argmax Pro: Frontier-level Real-time Speech-to-text with Speakers and Custom Vocabulary on Mobile Devices
items.abstract: We introduce Argmax Pro, a unified real-time inference system that orchestrates three state-of-the-art billion-scale transformer models for speech-to-text with speaker diarization and custom vocabulary. The system is optimized to run efficiently on a wide range of mobile devices across iOS and Android without resource contention with other apps and with minimal impact to battery life and thermals. The goal of this system is to offer a peer alternative to cloud-based systems for feature-rich speech recognition with frontier-level accuracy. To achieve this, we built Argmax Pro on top of concurrent research in context biasing and streaming speaker diarization.

items.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Companion for Real-Time Entity Extraction and SLU-Driven ASR Error Correction
items.abstract: Contact-center agents handle thousands of entity-rich voice interactions per day, where a misrecognised customer name, account identifier, or domain term cascades into wrong CRM entries and additional manual rework. We demonstrate MACE (Multi-Agent Companion Environment), a closed-loop architecture in which a real-time companion - an AI overlay that runs alongside the live agent and surfaces extracted named entities as proactive suggestions for in-place confirmation - routes every UI correction back into the ASR stack as either a contextual-biasing entry B or, once recurrent, a post-ASR substitution rule R, with no acoustic retraining and no a-priori entity list. On the English ContextASR-Bench benchmark with Whisper-large-v3, the loop reduces NE-WER by 17.1% and EditRate by 18.6% over a no-biasing baseline, closing 23.6% of the gap to an oracle that is given the entity list in advance.

items.title: AppTek Call-Center Dialogues: A Multi-Accent Long-Form Benchmark for English ASR
items.abstract: Evaluating English ASR systems for conversational AI applications remains difficult, as many publicly available corpora are either pre-segmented into short segments, consist of read or prepared speech, or lack explicit dialect annotations to evaluate robustness for a diverse user base. This work presents the AppTek Call-Center Dialogues corpus, a collection of spontaneous, role-played agent-customer conversations spanning fourteen English accents covering sixteen service-oriented scenarios. The dataset was commissioned specifically for evaluation and none of the audio or text was publicly available prior to release, reducing the risk of overlap with existing large-scale pretraining corpora. We benchmark a set of open-source ASR systems under different segmentation approaches. Results show substantial variation across accents and segmentation methods, indicating that good performance on general American English benchmarks does not necessarily generalize to other accents.

items.title: Segmental Attention Decoding With Long Form Acoustic Encodings
items.abstract: We address the fundamental incompatibility of attention-based encoder-decoder (AED) models with long-form acoustic encodings. AED trained on segmented utterances learn to encode absolute positions by exploiting limited acoustic context beyond segment boundaries, but fail to generalize when decoding long-form segments where these cues vanish. The model loses ability to order acoustic encodings due to permutation invariance of keys and values in cross-attention. We propose four modifications: 1) injecting explicit absolute positional encodings into cross-attention, 2) long-form training with extended acoustic context to eliminate implicit absolute position encoding, 3) segment concatenation to cover diverse segmentations needed during training, 4) semantic segmentation to align AED-decoded segments with training segments. We show that these modifications close the accuracy gap between continuous and segmented acoustic encodings, enabling auto-regressive use of the attention decoder.

items.title: M-LAMA: Multimodal Automated Scoring of Long-form Spoken English
items.abstract: Automatic speech assessment (ASA) for real-world exams requires evaluating multi-minute spontaneous responses across acoustic delivery, linguistic quality, and task fulfillment. However, most prior work focuses on short utterances, leaving long-form comprehensive assessment underexplored. We investigate whether reliable scoring of extended speech requires structured multimodal modeling. We propose M-LAMA, a cross-modal framework integrating raw audio, ASR transcripts, and question context through dual encoders and a discourse-aware fusion decoder. A part-based audio structure and question-aware text encoding capture both how and what is spoken, while a three-stage training strategy addresses the bell-curve score distribution of high-stakes exams. Experiments on 87,226 full-length sessions show that structured multimodal alignment substantially improves scoring reliability across five criteria, suggesting that effective long-form ASA requires principled integration of acoustic, linguistic, and contextual evidence.

items.title: Attentive Mamba: Channel-wise Local Attention for Speech Recognition
items.abstract: State space models (SSMs) have emerged as a powerful alternative to transformers for speech recognition, but the performance is constrained due to static local aggregation. This paper presents an attentive SSM that integrates a causal convolutional attention where the static convolution is upgraded with a channel-wise local attention. The proposed module first contextualizes queries, keys, and values via causal depth-wise convolutions before applying cross-channel attention over a temporally local window. This architecture is motivated by the inherent structure of speech spectrograms, where distinct frequency channels contain temporally coherent patterns that can benefit the channel-specific modeling prior to their integration. This design facilitates dynamic parameterization of the state transition matrices, leading to the expressive acoustic features. Experimental results confirm the merit of integrating dynamic channel-wise attention into SSM for speech recognition.

items.title: Attention-Guided Reliability Scaling for Contrastive Decoding in Robust Audio-Visual Speech Recognition
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based audio-visual speech recognition (AVSR) systems are robust under noise. Contrastive decoding (CD), originally introduced to stabilize LLM generation by contrasting a weaker model against a stronger one at inference time, adjusts predictions without additional training. In this work, we apply CD to AVSR by contrasting audio-only conditioning with full audio-visual conditioning within the same underlying model. However, using a fixed contrastive strength introduces a trade-off across noise levels: stronger intervention helps under severe noise but may over-correct reliable predictions in clean conditions. We propose reliability-aware scaling of CD for AVSR. Instead of using a fixed strength, we adaptively modulate the contrastive influence at each token based on reliability signals derived from attention dynamics and inter-model predictive divergence. Experiments on LRS3 show consistent improvements across clean and low-SNR conditions.

items.title: Listening with Attention: Entropy-Guided Explainability for Transformer-Based Audio Models
items.abstract: Transformer-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) models such as Whisper are highly accurate, but their predictions remain difficult to interpret. Existing explainable AI (XAI) methods often lack faithfulness and precise temporal grounding. We propose Listening with Entropy-guided Attention for Faithful eXplainability (LEAF-X), a model-intrinsic XAI framework for transformer-based ASR. LEAF-X combines entropy-guided attention weighting, multi-layer attention rollout, and optional causal ablations to identify low-entropy, high-impact heads and layers, producing sparse token-to-frame attributions. Unlike perturbation-based explainers or raw attention maps, LEAF-X exploits the internal structure of encoder-decoder and speech-augmented decoder-only models to generate explanations that better reflect model computation. Results show that LEAF-X produces more faithful and stable attributions than strong baselines, supporting more transparent and auditable ASR.

items.title: How Linguistic Dimension Interactions Shape Meaning Preservation in Multilingual ASR
items.abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition errors emerge from interactions across linguistic dimensions. While prior work correlated errors with external features, it remains unclear whether these patterns hold when linguistic features are measured from ASR outputs. We analysed substitution errors on the FLEURS dataset using Whisper and Seamless, computing phonetic, morphological, syntactic, and lexical similarity directly from ASR audio and transcriptions. Results revealed that semantic preservation emerges from systematic cross-dimension interactions: morphological and syntactic features operated interdependently while phonological accuracy intensified when syntax was preserved. Interaction patterns differed across architectures: Seamless showed better baseline performance, while Whisper showed heightened error sensitivity but leveraged morphological information more effectively, showing that ASR architectures integrate linguistic information through fundamentally different mechanisms.

items.title: Language-Aware Distillation for Multilingual Instruction-Following Speech LLMs with ASR-Only Supervision
items.abstract: Speech Large Language Models (LLMs) that understand and follow instructions in many languages are useful for real-world interaction, but are difficult to train with supervised fine-tuning, requiring large, task-specific speech corpora. While recent distillation-based approaches train performant English-only Speech LLMs using only annotated ASR data by aligning text and speech using only a lightweight projector, these models under-perform when scaled to multilingual settings due to language interference in the shared projector. We address this by introducing language-aware distillation using a query bank and a gating network that selects or mixes query tokens using a Q-Former projector. Our approach shows gains of 14% over matched multilingual distillation baselines on instruction following. We further synthesize Audio-MLQA, a multilingual spoken QA benchmark built on MLQA with high-quality TTS questions. Our best model improves over existing Speech LLM baselines by 32% on Audio-MLQA.

items.title: ERM-MinMaxGAP: Benchmarking and Mitigating Gender Bias in Multilingual Multimodal Speech-LLM Emotion Recognition
items.abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) systems can exhibit gender-related performance disparities, but how such bias manifests in multilingual speech LLMs across languages and modalities is unclear. We introduce a novel multilingual, multimodal benchmark built on MELD-ST, spanning English, Japanese, and German, to quantify language-specific SER performance and gender gaps. We find bias is strongly language-dependent, and multimodal fusion does not reliably improve fairness. To address these, we propose ERM-MinMaxGAP, a fairness-informed training objective, which augments empirical risk minimization (ERM) with a proposed adaptive fairness weight mechanism and a novel MinMaxGAP regularizer on the maximum male-female loss gap within each language and modality. Building upon the Qwen2-Audio backbone, our ERM-MinMaxGAP approach improves multilingual SER performance by 5.5% and 5.0% while reducing the overall gender bias gap by 0.1% and 1.4% in the unimodal and multimodal settings, respectively.

items.title: Confidence-Gated Mean-Teacher Consistency Regularization for Low-Resource Multilingual ASR with Shared–Private Fusion-LoRA
items.abstract: Low-resource multilingual ASR commonly relies on joint training, but excessive parameter sharing can cause negative transfer. Meanwhile, consistency learning as a remedy for limited labels may amplify cross-view instability and confirmation bias when predictions are unreliable. To tackle this, we propose a Whisper-based parameter-efficient framework. Architecturally, it adopts a shared-private Fusion-LoRA design (SPF-LoRA): a shared branch learns cross-lingual commonality, a private branch captures language-specific traits, and a learnable fusion weight adaptively balances both to mitigate multilingual interference. In training, we introduce a Mean-Teacher consistency regularization strategy (MT-CR), where an EMA teacher provides more stable consistency targets and reliability filtering suppresses noisy consistency signals. On Kathbath, we reduce macro WER by 35.4% over Whisper-small+LoRA, outperform the reported Whisper-medium+LoRA baseline, and improve all five languages.

items.title: Speech Encoder Fusion for LLM-based Automatic Speech Recognition
items.abstract: Speech-aware large language models (LLMs) can incorporate speech through pre-trained acoustic encoders that project speech features into the LLM embedding space. While the choice of the speech encoder critically influences performance, different encoders often exhibit complementary strengths, motivating their combination. In this work, we investigate whether fusing multiple pre-trained speech encoders can enhance speech-aware LLMs for automatic speech recognition (ASR). We explore several fusion strategies beyond simple feature concatenation, including learned combinations and Transformer-based fusion architectures, and evaluate them across mono- and multilingual ASR settings as well as diarized speech recognition. Our results indicate that carefully fusing multiple parallel speech encoders improves downstream performance in all scenarios with limited computational overhead.

items.title: Dissecting Sensitivity to Training Language in Self-Supervised Speech Learning Using Neural Audio Codec Tokens
items.abstract: Neural audio codecs (NACs) have become popular for obtaining speech representations as discrete tokens. Beyond compression, discrete tokens can be used to train self-supervised learning (SSL) models. Such models, referred to as codec-based SSL models, reduce data storage and computational cost, enabling scalable SSL pre-training. However, their language sensitivity remains unclear. When the language changes, codec-based SSL models may require retraining, which undermines their efficiency. In this paper, we present a systematic analysis of language sensitivity by varying either the NAC training language or the SSL pre-training language while keeping the other fixed. Experimental results show that downstream performance is insensitive to the NAC training language but strongly dependent on the SSL pre-training language. These findings suggest that a single NAC can be reused across languages, while aligning the SSL pre-training language with the target language is crucial.

items.title: SᴜTRA: Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness
items.abstract: Existing subword tokenizers optimize statistical compression but ignore morphological structure, particularly the relationship between roots and affixes. This is harmful for morphologically rich Indic languages, where basic units are complex orthographic syllables (aksharas) rather than letters. Frequency-based methods over-fragment words, arbitrarily splitting roots and affixes—a phenomenon we term Morphological Shattering. We propose SᴜTRA (Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness), a morphology-aware algorithm that preserves akshara indivisibility and penalizes merges crossing morphological boundaries. We also release a new morphological segmentation dataset for Hindi, Marathi, and Gujarati. SᴜTRA reduces shattering, achieving peak gains of +14.7% in morphological alignment (Boundary F1) and +34% in semantic recoverability (Hindi) over Bᴘᴇ. These structural gains yield an average improvement of +8.08 ᴄʜʀF2 in machine translation.

items.title: Measuring the Redundancy of Decoder Layers in SpeechLLMs
items.abstract: Speech Large Language Models route speech encoder representations into an LLM decoder that typically accounts for over 90% of total parameters. We study how much of this decoder capacity is actually needed for speech tasks. Across two LLM families and three scales (1-8B), we show that decoder redundancy is largely inherited from the pretrained LLM: text and speech inputs yield similar redundant blocks. We then measure excess capacity by pruning decoder layers and analysing post-pruning healing to increase robustness. Our findings show that 7-8B models retain good ASR performance with only ~60% of decoder layers, and the same trend extends to smaller scales with reduced pruning tolerance. We then generalise to speech translation, and show that the same blocks of layers are redundant across speech encoders, tasks and languages, indicating that a more global redundancy structure exists, enabling a single pruned SpeechLLM backbone to support multiple tasks at lower computational cost.

items.title: Weakly Masked Residual Reliability Learning for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Speech Models
items.abstract: This paper proposes a Weakly Masked Residual Reliability Learning (WMR2L) framework to enhance the robustness of speech models in cross-domain scenarios. WMR2L jointly models prediction confidence and residual dispersion for pseudo-label weighting, enabling the separation of reliable predictions from overconfident ones. To mitigate supervision bias introduced by selective pseudo-labeling, we propose a weak confidence masking strategy that partially masks high-confidence regions, thereby promoting learning from less reliable regions. In addition, a multi-perturbation consistency regularization is designed to further improve pseudo-label quality. Experimental results show that WMR2L consistently outperforms existing baselines across multiple cross-domain speech recognition tasks, achieving relative WER reductions of 13.8% on CHiME-4 (noisy), 25.0% on SLURP (human-machine interaction), and 15.7% on CORAAL (accented), and also yields notable improvements on speech translation tasks. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/ status/Speech-Model-Adaptation-8D45

items.title: Contrastive Training with LLM-generated Near-Misses for Robust Code-Switching Speech Recognition
items.abstract: Code-switching (CS), the alternation between multiple languages within a single utterance, remains challenging for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). To address this issue, we propose a Point-of-Interest (POI)-aware contrastive training framework that improves recognition at CS-critical regions. We first identify CS spans by adopting POI detection method from literature, then construct acoustically plausible near-miss hypotheses by perturbing POIs in ASR N-best outputs and expanding candidates with a large language model. Hard but plausible negatives are retained through filtering with acoustic, phonemic, and textual constraints. Finally, we fine-tune Whisper-small with LoRA using a POI-weighted cross-entropy anchor objective together with a multi-negative contrastive ranking loss. Experiments on CS-FLEURS (cmn-eng) and ViMedCSS (vie-eng) show consistent reductions of over 2% in both general and CS-aware error rates compared to standard LoRA fine-tuning.
